objects.original: Real-valued f, Euclidean gradient, and Hessian quadratic form.
objects.reconstructed: Real-valued f, gradient as the Riesz representative of Df, and D²f(x)[v,v] as two evaluations of fderiv (fderiv f).
objects.evidence: The actual module differentiates t ↦ Df(x+t v)[v]. In Euclidean space its derivative is the classical Hessian quadratic form; real inner-product symmetry accounts for the source pairing order. No independently postulated Hessian or gradient is substituted.

domains.evidence: The domain extension is explicit in the module preamble, lesson and candidate_assumptions. Both directions use scalar differentiation and integration along a segment; neither compactness of the ambient space nor finite-dimensional Hessian matrices is used.

quantifiers.original: For each fixed nonnegative m, equivalence of all-pairs gradient monotonicity and the Hessian bound at all points and directions.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For each fixed arbitrary real m, the same two globally quantified conditions.
quantifiers.evidence: The scope of x,y,x,v agrees. The only parameter-quantifier extension is from m≥0 to all real m. The identical fixed m is retained on both sides; it is not allowed to depend on the points or directions.

assumptions.original: C² on ℝ^d, with m≥0 inherited from Proposition 1.6.
assumptions.reconstructed: ContDiff ℝ 2 f on a complete real inner-product space, with no sign assumption on m.
assumptions.evidence: The omitted sign restriction is deliberate and disclosed by candidate_assumptions and lesson assumption 3. In the forward proof only positive t is cancelled; neither m nor the direction norm is divided by. The reverse proof integrates an inequality against positive measure, valid also for negative m. C² supplies all derivative and interval-integrability requirements.

conclusion.reconstructed: The same quantitative gradient/Hessian equivalence in Fréchet notation.
conclusion.evidence: Forward: at x+t v, t>0 gives t²m‖v‖² ≤ t(g(t)−g(0)); two positive cancellations give m‖v‖² ≤ (g(t)−g(0))/t. The genuine right derivative at zero supplies D²f(x)[v,v]. Reverse: integrate the Hessian bound along x+t(y−x) and use the reviewed scalar FTC identity.

scopes.original: Global, pointwise inequalities equivalent under C²; source uses a positive directional limit and the segment FTC.
scopes.reconstructed: Global, pointwise inequalities in an iff, established by the same right-limit and integral mechanisms.
scopes.evidence: All points and directions are unrestricted, including zero displacement. No conclusion is assumed as a premise: hf is the only regularity premise, hm and hH are introduced separately within the respective implication branches.

constant_dependencies.original: The same nonnegative m multiplies the squared norm in both inequalities.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same signed m multiplies the same squared norms, with no dimension factor.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Integration is over an interval of length one, so ∫₀¹m‖v‖²dt=m‖v‖². The source modulus α is renamed m without scaling; the sign-domain extension is recorded in assumptions and quantifiers.

deltas.description: The equivalence is proved on complete real Hilbert spaces, beyond the finite-dimensional source.
deltas.evidence: The typeclasses, lesson and scoped assumptions all state the extension.

deltas.description: The reusable equivalence permits negative m, whereas the source proposition assumes a nonnegative modulus.
deltas.evidence: Only the positive segment parameter is cancelled, and the converse uses monotonicity of integration; the proof remains valid for signed m. The publication lesson explicitly says any real m.
